title: No anonymous-access regression coverage for test push route
reasoning: The route exposes a network POST endpoint that enqueues a push notification task for the current user. The included tests only exercise authenticated clients via force_authenticate and successful task enqueue/default-message behavior; they never assert that an anonymous request is rejected. Because this endpoint has a side effect, losing or omitting authentication on TestPushNotificationView would allow unauthenticated callers to trigger push task work and the current linked tests would not catch it.
recommendation: Add explicit authentication/permission coverage for notifications:test-push-notification, asserting anonymous POSTs return 401 or 403 and do not call send_push_notification_task.delay.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: TestPushNotificationTests authenticates the APIClient in setUp before every request and contains only success/default-message/no-token cases, all expecting HTTP 200 and a queued task call.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a test that uses a fresh unauthenticated APIClient, POSTs to reverse('notifications:test-push-notification'), asserts status is 401/403, and asserts send_push_notification_task.delay was not called.
